questions.answer: The first query selects students with at least one enrollment; the recursive CTE generates numbers from 1 through 5.
questions.explanation:
The first query selects students with at least one enrollment; the recursive CTE generates numbers from 1 through 5.
Why: A subquery runs inside another query; a correlated subquery can refer to a value from the outer row. EXISTS tests whether a subquery returns at least one row and is useful for finding related records. A CTE names an intermediate result with WITH, while WITH RECURSIVE can walk hierarchies step by step. A CTE usually exists only for that statement; it is not automatically a stored table.
